author: Greg McVerry
body_html:
Just read the marketing material from Watermark (@TK20/askstream). We just screw up dispositions assessments. First rubrics are not reliable. Each scoring session needs a reliability test. Different raters different subjects. The study I saw (can't share its NDAd) called STRONG reliability as (.60 to .26) Guess standards have fallen in terms of what counts as strong. Also I would never accept for publication a validation and reliability study that only reports Pearson's correlation coefficient. Chance error anyone?

The cited validation study wasn't included in citations. http://go.galegroup.com/ps/i.do?id=GALE%7CA278759337&sid=googleScholar&v=2.1&it=r&linkaccess=fulltext&issn=00131172&p=AONE&sw=w

When I found it the instrument validated had nothing to do with the study. I saw no EFA, No CFA. Just told CAEP approves it so the data doesn't really matter.
